concept: Aero protocol and Slipstream integration for LP automation
summary: Source-anchored research for Aero protocol and Slipstream integration for LP automation. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: The source CLGaugeFactory defaults are DEFAULT_MIN_STAKE_BLOCKS = 5 and a DEFAULT_PENALTY_RATE equal to MAX_PIPS. Gauge divides the penalty by MAX_PIPS imported from contracts/libraries/ProtocolConstants.sol, where that constant represents 100%, so the default early reward forfeit is the entire reward. Gauge applies the rate when the current block is below depositBlock plus minStakeBlocks. This is a block window, not a fixed wall-clock duration, and these defaults are not an attestation of current live configuration. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

CLGaugeFactory source defines DEFAULT_MIN_STAKE_BLOCKS = 5 and a DEFAULT_PENALTY_RATE equal to MAX_PIPS. Gauge divides the penalty by MAX_PIPS imported from ProtocolConstants.sol, where that constant represents 100%, so the constructor defaults are a five-block window and a full reward penalty. These are constructor defaults, not verified live Base settings or a fixed wall-clock duration. (medium confidence)

CoinGecko assigns the Aero Slipstream (Base) exchange API ID `aero-slipstream-base`. Use this venue identifier when selecting Base Slipstream markets in CoinGecko data. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05)

The interface NatSpec assumes an existing initialized pool, but the implementation additionally calls createPool when sqrtPriceX96 is nonzero. For an existing pool, set sqrtPriceX96 to zero; the factory requires the pool mapping to be empty before creation. The implementation therefore supports a creation branch omitted by that NatSpec. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05)

Fee revenue follows the liquidity reward mode: the Slipstream reference says captured MEV follows ordinary trading-fee routing, reaching token operators for AERO-earning liquidity and LPs for fee-earning liquidity. Treat fee income and AERO emissions as different modes when evaluating a range strategy. (low confidence)

Aero `getAmountsForLiquidity` returns only token0 when the current square-root price is at or below the lower bound, both assets strictly between bounds, and only token1 at or above the upper bound. Use current pool price and position liquidity to value principal; this helper does not add uncollected fees or emissions. (low confidence)

For an unstaked NFT with nonzero liquidity, `collect` first pokes the pool with a zero-liquidity burn and adds each inside-fee-growth delta multiplied by position liquidity and divided by `FixedPoint128.Q128` to the stored owed balance. When position liquidity is zero, `collect` skips that poke and fee-growth update and collects only from the stored owed balances. For a position with liquidity, stored `tokensOwed0` and `tokensOwed1` alone can omit fees accrued since the previous update. (low confidence)

For a staked NFT, `positions` substitutes current pool inside-fee growth for the returned fee checkpoint. When the position has nonzero liquidity, `collect` refreshes the stored fee-growth snapshot from the gauge-owned pool position without adding a fresh fee-growth delta to the NFT owed balances; with zero liquidity it skips that refresh. Applying the unstaked fee formula blindly to a gauge-owned NFT can misclassify its earnings. (low confidence)

The `earned` function in CLGauge projects unsettled cumulative gauge rewards into pool reward growth in memory when active staked liquidity exists. It validates position ownership, applies penalty before referral share, and adds account-level `deferredEmissions`. Treat this result as an account estimate including deferred withdrawals, not simply the gross rewards of the currently selected NFT. (low confidence)

The published CLGaugeFactory constructor defaults are `DEFAULT_MIN_STAKE_BLOCKS = 5` and a `DEFAULT_PENALTY_RATE` equal to `MAX_PIPS`. Gauge divides the penalty by `MAX_PIPS` imported from `ProtocolConstants.sol`, where that constant represents 100%, so the default early penalty is the full accrued reward. Gauge applies the configured rate only while the current block is strictly below deposit block plus the minimum, so the boundary block is eligible without that penalty. These are source defaults, not a verified live Base configuration. (medium confidence)

Read `effectivePenaltyConfig` for the target gauge before scheduling a claim or rebalance: the factory penalty administrator can change the factory minimum and rate, and can override the minimum for an individual gauge. A zero per-gauge override falls back to the factory minimum. Source defaults therefore cannot establish the target gauge's current holding period or forfeit percentage. (low confidence)

Aero describes Markets figures as comparison estimates rather than onchain values. Stake APR estimates what Allocation Power directed to a pool earns; it should not be substituted for the return of a concentrated LP position. (low confidence)

CoinGecko identifies the migrated Aero coin with API ID `aero` and states that it migrated from an old contract to a new contract. Resolve the migrated asset explicitly rather than selecting it by the shared AERO symbol. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05)

CoinGecko reports that circulating supply for the migrated Aero token is not reported. Treat this as missing provider data rather than evidence that the token has no circulating supply. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05)

CoinGecko documents the coins/markets endpoint for coin-level market data. Its response includes nullable current price and total volume and a last-update timestamp; these fields describe a coin rather than a particular Aero pool. (low confidence)

CoinGecko warns that an unverified token market cap returns null and that pool addresses absent from GeckoTerminal are ignored. A missing result therefore requires a coverage check rather than treating it as a zero-valued market. (low confidence)

The May 8 FAQ retains a September 2026 launch target, whereas the upgrade hub records the actual October 21 EDT launch; the former is a historical forecast rather than the final launch date. (low confidence)

CLGauge inherits deposit(uint256) and withdraw(uint256) from Gauge. Reward calls are claimEmissions(address,address) and claimEmissions(address,address,uint256[]), authorized for the account or an approved claim operator. Verify reward-claim method names against this ABI instead of importing them from legacy Slipstream integrations. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05)

The docs describe CL1, CL50, CL100, CL200 and CL2000. Independently decoding the Base deployment clFactoryConstructorArgs as ABI words yields seven initial tick-spacing and fee entries, including intermediate classes and no CL2000 entry. CLFactory enables the initial fee tiers passed to its constructor. These published artifacts disagree; query the target factory for currently enabled spacings instead of using the documentation table as an exhaustive allowlist. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05)

The dynamic hook caches a block-wide fee set on the first swap in each block. Unless the pool's configured base fee is ZERO_FEE_INDICATOR, that first swap recomputes the dynamic component from recent oracle tick history and stores the base fee plus that dynamic component, capped at the fee cap; a zero base fee falls back to the tick-spacing fee. When the base fee is ZERO_FEE_INDICATOR, the first swap instead uses and stores the static tick-spacing fee and computes no dynamic component. Caller discounts and initial-transaction handling can alter the applied fee, and beforeSwap adds the MEV module fee. The tick-spacing fee is therefore an input to the charged fee rather than a fixed execution quote. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Aero documents five tick-spacing classes: CL1 (1), CL50 (50), CL100 (100), CL200 (200), and CL2000 (2000). Its quoted grid widths are approximate, and the documentation allows future classes; these labels identify spacing rather than a fixed swap-fee percentage. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05)

Pool identity includes the token pair and tick spacing. The factory rejects duplicate pools for that key, exposes tickSpacings(), and lets its owner enable additional spacings; a bot should discover enabled spacings rather than hard-code a permanently closed list. (low confidence)

`decreaseLiquidity` credits removed principal to `tokensOwed0` and `tokensOwed1` and also credits fee-growth deltas, then reduces position liquidity. `collect` subsequently transfers from the owed balances. A bot must distinguish withdrawn principal from fee income instead of treating the entire collect amount as yield. (low confidence)

The CL pool credits realized emissions to `rewardGrowthGlobalX128` per unit of active staked liquidity. With no active staked liquidity it banks emissions in rollover instead. CLGauge computes each position reward as inside reward-growth delta times its liquidity divided by `Q128`; the claim path forfeits returned rollover rather than awarding that idle-period accrual to a later depositor. (medium confidence)

CoinGecko documents `/onchain/networks/{network}/pools/{address}` for an individual network and pool address, with pool-level volume and reserve value. This is the pool-specific data interface to evaluate separately from coin-level market data. (low confidence)
The Aero upgrade hub states that Aerodrome and Velodrome became Aero on October 21, 2026 at 8:00 PM EDT, equivalent to October 22 at 00:00 UTC. (low confidence)

Aero identifies MetaDEX03 as its DEX operating system from Dromos Labs; the public MetaDEX repository covers AMM pools, voting escrow, gauges, rewards, cross-chain messaging, Metarouter, and Relay. (medium confidence)
The upgrade hub lists Base among the seven launch networks, together with Ethereum Mainnet, OP Mainnet, Arc, Ink, Robinhood Chain, and Arbitrum. (low confidence)
sAERO is staked AERO replacing veAERO and veVELO; its holders direct AERO Rewards to pools and earn Exchange Revenue from those pools. (low confidence)
The upgrade hub and Bitget migration notice agree that old AERO converts to new AERO at 1:1, while each VELO (called VELODROME by Bitget) converts to 0.044 new AERO. (medium confidence)
The upgrade hub says legacy Aerodrome and Velodrome emissions stopped at launch and that earning new AERO Rewards as an LP requires upgrading. (low confidence)

Bitget's October 27 notice scheduled its AERO deposit and withdrawal suspension for November 2, 2026 at 03:00 UTC; this is the exchange migration schedule, distinct from the protocol launch. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)

The MetaDEX repository says new protocol files use Dromos Restricted Use License 1.0, which does not allow production use; each version converts to GPL-2.0-or-later five years after first public distribution, while interfaces are MIT unless they inherit GPL. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05)

The Aero Security Overview and Base deployment JSON agree on the position manager 0x4857DB576eE0e45F10525eC59527BfD10beeC60b, CL factory 0x9CB220581b91b0C83223012FE69688b92aD07a76, and CL gauge factory 0xf437f62053ACB121665b8fDBfeA8F214FB8E589d. Treat these as published deployment records; this research did not check deployed bytecode. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05)

The exact mint tuple field order and types are: address token0, address token1, int24 tickSpacing, int24 tickLower, int24 tickUpper, uint256 amount0Desired, uint256 amount1Desired, uint256 amount0Min, uint256 amount1Min, address recipient, uint256 deadline, uint160 sqrtPriceX96. The payable mint returns uint256 tokenId, uint128 liquidity, uint256 amount0, uint256 amount1. Generate the ABI from this interface. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05)

Depositing requires NFT ownership and NFT approval to the gauge, verifies that the position tokens and tick spacing match, collects fees, and transfers custody to the gauge. A normal withdrawal attempts to claim emissions, removes staked liquidity, and returns the NFT to the caller. Finish withdrawal before using a wallet-owned position-manager removal recipe. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05)

Read effectivePenaltyConfig(gauge) before planning claims or a rebalance. Factory administrators can change the common penalty rate and holding window, and gauges can have a holding-window override. The explicit claim path also applies the effective penalty through _computePositionEmissions; waiting to withdraw does not make an earlier claim penalty-free. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05)

The Sugar Base deployment env file publishes LP_SUGAR_ADDRESS_8453=0x69dD9db6d8f8E7d83887A704f447b1a584b599A1 and TOKEN_SUGAR_8453=0x910CD56277994B4970F49AEDA52c96aD620aE81D, but its configured voter is 0x16613524e02ad97eDfeF371bC883F2F5d6C480A5 and its CL factory list excludes Aero CLFactory 0x9CB220581b91b0C83223012FE69688b92aD07a76. Aero's published Base contract-address table instead lists Voter 0x49d7d4f17Ec56Ef8fA04E464AF5D1A4942CC31e6. These records do not establish that this Sugar deployment indexes Aero; do not certify it as Aero-compatible from the chain ID alone. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05)

The position-manager interface exposes decreaseLiquidity with tokenId, liquidity, amount0Min, amount1Min and deadline; collect with tokenId, recipient, amount0Max and amount1Max; and burn only after liquidity and collectible amounts are empty. A range exit therefore needs distinct decrease and collection operations. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05)

Viem simulateContract obtains return data and revert reasons for contract writes without changing chain state. Use it with the Aero ABI and actual caller before submitting the corresponding write; simulation is a preflight check and does not reserve the simulated state. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05)

Slipstream concentrates liquidity between chosen lower and upper ticks. A position becomes inactive outside its range; waiting for price to return is an alternative to repositioning. (medium confidence)

Aero describes dynamic fees as a volatility multiplier that raises the base fee in volatile markets and relaxes toward it in calm markets. The auditor guide identifies DynamicSwapFeeHook as the CL fee hook, including the priority-fee MEV tax; the implementation supports default and per-pool swap hooks. (medium confidence)

Slipstream deposits are ERC-721 positions. Gauge deposit checks the position token pair and tick spacing, transfers the NFT into gauge custody, stakes its liquidity, and records depositBlock. This makes the holding-period stamp specific to the staked NFT. (medium confidence)

Penalty configuration is mutable: effectivePenaltyConfig(gauge) combines the factory penalty rate with the gauge minimum stake blocks. A zero gauge override falls back to the factory minimum. Read this configuration before scheduling a reward claim or exit. (medium confidence)

The early-penalty test uses block height: while _blockNumber() < depositBlock + minStakeBlocks, a positive penalty rate subtracts reward * penaltyRate / MAX_PIPS. CLGauge applies this inside _computePositionEmissions on ordinary claims as well as withdrawals; claiming before maturity does not bypass the penalty. (medium confidence)

The public auditor guide records two fee-hook limitations: initialFee can be consumed by a small swap before a larger swap in the same block, and a zero beforeSwap return falls back to the static tick-spacing fee. These are attributed known-issue statements in the guide, not a fresh exploit demonstration or proof of current deployed behavior. (low confidence)

For principal valuation, let L be position liquidity and a < s < b be normalized lower, current and upper square-root prices. The in-range amounts are token0 = L*(b-s)/(s*b) and token1 = L*(s-a). Aero implements these in `getAmountsForLiquidity` with fixed-point integer helpers; Uniswap documents the same in-range formulas. (medium confidence)

Aero `getLiquidityForAmounts` uses the token0 budget below the range and the token1 budget above it. In range it computes candidate liquidity from each token budget and takes the smaller value; desired deposit amounts therefore need not both be fully consumed. (low confidence)

In the pool source, mixed-liquidity fee splitting first rounds up the staked share of swap fees, then rounds up an additional `unstakedFee()` levy on the remaining fee share using denominator of one million. The residual fee growth is divided only by unstaked active liquidity. If all active liquidity is staked, all swap fees go to gauge fees; a fee-earning LP does not necessarily retain its entire pro-rata swap fee share. (low confidence)

The official documentation describes MinStake forfeiture on early withdrawal. The CLGauge source additionally applies the same penalty through an ordinary emissions claim while the NFT remains staked: `_claimPositions` invokes `_computePositionEmissions`, which advances the growth checkpoint and applies `_applyPenalty`. Early claiming can therefore permanently forfeit the accrued slice without withdrawing principal; withdrawal-only wording is incomplete for bot scheduling. (low confidence)

On deposit, CLGauge collects existing pool fees to the credited owner, transfers the NFT into gauge custody, stakes its liquidity, and records both an inside-reward-growth checkpoint and `depositBlock`. Ordinary reward computation updates the growth checkpoint but does not reset the deposit block. A new deposit after withdrawal stamps a new holding-period start. (low confidence)

The normal CLGauge withdrawal path collects fees, attempts to claim emissions, then unstakes liquidity and returns the NFT. If emission minting reverts, `_claimOrDeferPositionEmissions` records net LP rewards in account-level `deferredEmissions` for a later claim; a successful NFT withdrawal therefore need not imply a successful emission payout. (low confidence)
